title: Macro Defect Inspection - Haze Detection on Teron 640
subtitle: Post-Implant Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Priya Sharma

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron 640 system to detect and classify Haze defects during post-implant inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 15 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Haze defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron 640 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron 640
- Inspection Type: Macro Defect Inspection
- Target Defect: Haze
- Process Step: Post-Implant
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 15

This test case applies to all Teron 640 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 15 for post-implant monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron 640
Software Version: v13.7.511
Recipe: MACRO_DEFECT_INSPECTION_28nm_POST_IMPLANT
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (79 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron 640 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Macro Defect Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Haze defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 119 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 95% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.7% for Macro Defect Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.94 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-04-25
Wafers Tested: 14
Total Defects Found: 2567
Defect Density: 363.16 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 1.6%
Capture Rate: 86.0%
Test Duration: 47 minutes
System Uptime: 97.5%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron 640 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Haze at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Throughput metrics met production requirements without sensitivity compromise.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
